census._about: (0.4.3, gamefixes: every NPC of the lore registered, spawned in their kingdom, with their documented occupation, home, workplace and bed) ShadowVeil's people as projectrpg.txt lists them under 'NPCs Present', one entry each: a one-word name (titles in 'title'), their kingdom, the Npc role and profession that drive their behaviour, the registry structure that is their home and the one that is their workplace (null home: the one exception, the bounty hunter). An entry with a 'body' is played by the roster person of that Ids constant (renamed and re-dressed on ShadowVeil; the devmap keeps its own people); every other entry is made for ShadowVeil alone, numbered from Ids.SV_PEOPLE in this order. Until the interiors come (0.4.4) each person keeps exterior stand-ins: a home stage and a work stage on open ground before their buildings' doors, where they arrive home, wait at work and go in for the night; their bed is planned inside their home's reserved interior and kept in the registry.

stage._about: How far before a doorway its stand-ins lie (cells), how far apart people sharing one stand side by side, and when the townsfolk turn in and come out (hours).

kits._about: What a person made for ShadowVeil carries and how able they are, by role (then by profession where it says so): skill levels, worn kit, and items in the pack.

stations._about: The workstations each calling needs at its workplace (Recipes.Station names), set out in the open before the workplace until its interior comes - one of each kind per workplace, shared by everyone who works there.

fields._about: (0.4.3, gamefixes: farms did not work or have their crops) every field and garden the architecture raised is farmed: its rows sown with its kingdom's crops (row by row, cycling), kept by the crop farmer the census sets to work there - else the nearest crop farmer of its kingdom within 'reach' cells - or, with nobody to keep it, open to anyone. 'unfarmed' names the ones that are not (the vineyard's vines).

posts._about: (0.4.4) Where each person stands to work inside their workplace: the kinds of post they take there, in the order they want them - by words of their title first, then by calling, then by role. A post is one the interiors set out (teller, clerk, counter, bar, cook, kitchen, altar, desk, jailer, guard, head, throne, mill, station:<STATION>); 'station:' alone takes any station. Whoever finds none works out of doors as before.

census._additions: (0.4.4, gamefixes: ten more people across the map) The people who keep the new jails, banks and graveyards, after the lore's own roll (kept apart so the roll's generator never drops them): each made for ShadowVeil alone, numbered after the roll. (0.4.5, gamefixes: 225 people) Ten more of the wilds: four of Garmund's band at his camp, three prospectors in the mines' bunkhouses, two loggers at the Loggers' Rest and a charcoal burner at the clamps.

honorifics._about: (0.4.4) The honorific a person's name carries, by a word of their title (male, female), else by their role: a knight is Sir or Dame, a lord by their rank, a priest Father or Mother.

outfits._about: (0.4.5, gamefixes: the clothing update; everyone but the townsfolk in gear that can be seen and looted) What each person wears of the outfits (data/apparel.json), the first that applies: by name, by where they live, by calling, by role, then by kingdom (by title words, by role, else its default) for those of the kingdom not in arms. A slot the kit already filled (a guard's helm, a knight's plate) keeps what the kit put there; where an outfit has two pieces for one slot (the Desert's legs and robes), the rank decides ('robesFor').
